To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sectoral patterns in technical change can be categorized and explained in terms of whether a sector is (1) supplier dominated, (2) production intensive or (3) science based. (Author/MP)

the sources of knowledge used by firms in their innovations, the size of firms and the sectors to which they apply their innovations, and the sectors in which they are located are interrelated in systematic ways, and the interrelationships are explained by the taxonomy.

the sources, nature, and impacts of innovations and the characteristics of firms that produce them vary significantly across sectors, which is due in part to the differences in the sources of knowledge applied by firms and in their patterns of diversification and in part to the nature of the products and processes that are produced and applied in each sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sources of technological change and its impact on the economy, and the way in which the sources vary across sectors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the production of technology is a complex, dynamic process; (2) the sectoral patterns in the production and use of technology are diverse, reflecting the different sources, natures, and impacts of innovations and the characteristics of the firms that produce them; (3) the sources of innovation are not exogenous; (4) the sources of process innovation are diverse and reflect sectoral patterns; (5) the sources of product innovation are diverse and also reflect sectoral patterns.
the sectoral taxonomy proposed in this paper provides a basis for the development of a new theory of technical change, and for the development of the theory of the firm.
the sectoral patterns are a result of the different sources of knowledge and the different ways in which knowledge is transferred and applied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sectoral patterns approach to technical change is a useful framework for understanding the sources of technical change and the nature of the innovations and innovating companies.

the sectoral patterns in technical change are not only the product of the nature of the knowledge base of a sector, but also reflect a complex interaction among firms and sectors, in which the technological diversification and the technological trajectories of innovating firms are determined.
we have developed a taxonomy of sectoral patterns of innovation, based on a set of empirical regularities, and have developed a theory that explains the regularities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of technology is endogenous and that it can be systematically studied.
there are three different types of sectoral patterns of innovation and that these patterns can be used as the basis for a theory of technical change.
the sources of technical change and the nature of the innovations that result from them are sector specific.
